stories.title: Mapping thorium's preferred sites could pave the way for nuclear clocks
stories.desc: For decades, physicists have used a technique called Mössbauer spectroscopy to peer inside solid materials, revealing fine details of their surroundings by studying how their atomic nuclei absorb and re-emit gamma rays.

stories.title: Vacuum-fluctuation-enhanced superconductivity demonstrated for the first time
stories.desc: In a study published in Nature on Aug. 19, a research team has enhanced superconductivity through vacuum fluctuations for the first time. The achievement marks a significant advance in controlling quantum states of matter.

stories.title: How fusion reactions can survive flaws—up to a point
stories.desc: Researchers at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) have found that implosions designed for inertial fusion energy (IFE) can tolerate significant imperfections before performance abruptly declines, a finding that could inform the design of fuel targets for future fusion power plants.
